## Sampling Frame

You probably won't use any code to create your frame (maybe??). But you definitely need to read your frame into R for the next two steps.

:::callout-warning
Throughout the code below, replace `STRAT_VAR` with the name of the variable defining your strata in your data.
:::

```{r}
## read in sampling frame

frame <- read_csv("") |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |>  # clean up column names
  mutate(STRAT_VAR = factor(STRAT_VAR)) # turn your strata variable into a factor variable
```

Check the order of your strata -- if you want them in a different order change the order of the levels NOW!!

```{r}
levels(frame$STRAT_VAR)
```

pop_sizes

## Stratified Random Sample

Since we have chosen exact strata samples to use based on our calculations above, the R code in the slides before doesn't work. 

This `strata()` function is from the *sampling* package loaded in the beginning of the file.



### Find your sample

The function we are going to use uses the rownumber as an ID, so to make sure everything lines up and is matched up in the end, let's create an ID variable in the sampling frame.

```{r}
# creating a sampling ID which is just the row number
# you don't need to do anything here

frame <- frame |> 
  mutate(sampling_ID = row_number())
```

In the code below:

- Replace`"STRAT_VAR"` with the name of your stratification variable, in quotation marks.
- `size` is the VECTOR of your rounded $n_g$ strata sizes, determined above. Make sure this is in the order of your strata!! 
- You can change the seed if you want

```{r}
# stratified random sample
set.seed(343938)

mysample <- strata(data = frame,
                 stratanames = c("STRAT_VAR"),
                 size = c(),
                 method = "srswor")
```

```{r}
# CHECK that this worked as you anticipated

mysample |> 
  count(STRAT_VAR) 
```

Once you have confirmed that worked correctly, move on to adding this informaiton to your sampling frame.

### Add information back to your sampling frame

```{r}
# save a dataset with a new variable indicating that that islander is in the sample

sampleids <- mysample |> 
  select(ID_unit, STRAT_VAR) |> 
  mutate(in_sample = "yes")
```

```{r}
frame_with_sample <- frame |> 
  left_join(sampleids, 
            by = join_by(sampling_ID == ID_unit, 
                         STRAT_VAR)) 
```

Let's save the full sampling frame with this information

```{r}
write_csv(frame_with_sample, file = "lab4-frame-stratified-sample.csv")
```

Let's also save your sample!! Change the name of the file or where it is saved according to your setup. This will help you for collecting data.

```{r}
strat_sample <- frame_with_sample |> 
  filter(in_sample == "yes")

write_csv(strat_sample, file = "lab4-stratified-sample.csv")
```
